answer: Every submission must name 3 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. The echo graph is validated at intake and the river frontier is published, so that the ancestry of every answer is public, and reef anchors the chain at a checkpoint. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 375 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
